expected.meetingPurpose: Review Allotment Society site issues, agree practical maintenance tasks and confirm upcoming administration and event arrangements.
meetingObjectives: Confirm repair action for the broken water butt tap.
Address the damaged railway-side boundary fence and related safety concern.
Agree plot-fee and waiting-list administration updates.
Plan annual show arrangements and publicity.
Discuss the shed break-in and improve site security.
expected.executiveSummary: The committee worked through a set of operational site issues and agreed several practical follow-up tasks. Maintenance actions were assigned for the water butt, boundary fence and shed security. Administrative updates were also agreed for plot fees and waiting-list allocation, alongside planning for the annual show. The main risk left open is continued site-security exposure if break-ins persist.
discussion: Damaged railway-side boundary fence and associated safety risk.
Increase in annual plot fees from GBP 25 to GBP 30.
Allocation of three vacant plots from the waiting list.
Annual show date, categories and publicity.
GBP 50 budget for show prizes and rosettes.
Communal shed break-in and stolen equipment.
Ongoing site-security risk if break-ins continue.

actions.action: Replace the broken water butt tap on Saturday.
Photograph the damaged boundary fence and write to the council this week, copying in the councillor.
Update the renewal letter to reflect the GBP 30 annual plot fee from January.
Email the top three people on the waiting list by the end of the week, giving them 14 days to accept a plot.
Prepare the annual show schedule, categories and entry form, and publish them on the noticeboard and Facebook by mid-August.
Buy and fit a new hasp, padlock and solar alarm on Saturday, keeping spend under GBP 50.
